chapter_theme: Pazhamudircholai (பழமுதிர்சோலை, 1 of 2): Murugan of the hill of Solaimalai is hymned as the letter A and the form above the three gods, and as the guru who teaches Siva; the poet confesses courtesans who sell their love and polish brass for gold, the life from womb to old age taken as eternal, the old body coughing over its medicines and the sick body fattened on food, and asks for the feet, for servanthood, for the yogic ascent and for the knowledge that he is Siva.
structure_note: Courtesan songs (1308, 1311, 1312, 1315, 1317, 1319, 1320); songs on attachment, the life-course and the body (1310, 1314, 1316, 1321); doctrinal songs (1307 on Murugan as all, 1313 on the yogic ascent through the centres, 1318 on nada, bindu and Siva). 1309 is a short plea for the dance of knowledge. The hill is also called குலகிரி (1321, and 1322 in the next chapter) and அலையாமலை (1314); 1312's praise describes the town with its stream and towers.

1307.reading: Murugan is hymned as the letter A, the lord, the excess and the within; as Brahma, Vishnu and Hara and the one above them; as the letter I, as all things and as sweetness; and the poet asks him to run ahead of him so that even a lowly one may live on this wide earth. The praise names the form that delights Indra, the lord who rejoices in the worship the forest hunter offered at Kathirkamam, and the peacock that dances to the drum syllables, at Pazhamudircholai.
1307.nuance: அகரமுமாகி ... இகரமுமாகி: Murugan as the first letters, the image the Kural opens with; here he is also அவர்மேலாய், above the three gods he becomes. The plea is small and tender: எனது முன் ஓடி வரவேணும், run ahead of me. The praise names கதிர்காமம், the shrine in Lanka, and the hunter's worship there.

1308.reading: The poet describes the musk-smeared breasts, laughing play and many kinds of pleasure of women in love-union, and asks whether he, sunk in that union and given to low deeds, will ever reach the wisdom of jnana he has thought of. The praise is a long litany of the Goddess, Kali, the trident-bearer, Bhairavi, Nili, Varahi, Bhagavati, the poison-eater, Abhirami, Kapali who takes offerings, the yogini, the supremely auspicious, the chaste wife of the world, the knower of the Veda, whose son Murugan is, the hero who rushed at Sura and his army, at Pazhamudircholai.
1308.nuance: The praise is almost wholly the Goddess's names (கொலைபுரி காளி சூலி ... வேத ஞானி), fierce and gentle together, before புதல்வோனே makes Murugan her son. மதராஜன் கலவி: the union is called Kama's own.

1309.reading: A short song: the poet asks Murugan to come on earth for a purpose, so that Death does not come near and he may see the way, and to come performing the dance of knowledge that Narayana and Brahma never knew. The praise names him the bridegroom of the elephant-raised girl, the six-faced one with twelve eyes, the vel that destroyed Sura's kin, at Solaimalai.
1309.nuance: நாரணனும் வேதன் முன்பு தெரியாத ஞான நடம்: the dance that Vishnu and Brahma could not see is the idiom of Siva's unseen form, here given to Murugan's dance. ஆரமுதமான தந்தி மணவாளா: Devayanai, raised by the elephant.

1310.reading: The poet confesses that his heart wavered in desire for mother, father, wife, house, children and wealth, that through evil maya he took this life for permanent, and that, his earnings gone, he wandered the streets wasting away for women; he asks Murugan to come on the living peacock so that he may bow at the feet, and to show love that ends his deluding karma. The praise names the hero who defeated Sura, honoured in a land of fields and golden terraces like the gods' own town, who spoke the fitting word so that his father, the poison-throated dancer of the hall, rejoiced, at Solaimalai.
1310.nuance: The attachments come in order, kin and household and wealth before women: மாதுமனை யான மைந்தர் சேருபொருள் ஆசை. வாழ்வு சதமாம் இது: the error is to take life as eternal. ஆனமொழியே பகர்ந்து, the word that delighted Siva, points to the teaching of Siva without naming Om.

1311.reading: The poet confesses he was deluded by the spear eyes of women versed in the love-texts, did their bidding at their sweet words, grew mad with love, and when his great wealth had gone to them stood a sinner; he asks when he will seek and bow at the flower feet with anklets and kadamba. The praise names Murugan raised by the grace of Uma who holds the left of Siva, the nephew of the dark one who measured the earth with one step, and the vel that ground Sura's kin to dust, on the peacock that flies over the groves to Solaimalai.
1311.nuance: நீடு பொருள் போன பின்பு பாதகனுமாகி: the wealth spent on the women leaves him not only poor but a sinner. வீரமதனூல் விளம்பு போக மடமாதர்: the women are cast as teachers of Kama's treatise. Vishnu measuring the world (ஓரடியினால் அளந்த) is the Trivikrama story.

1312.reading: The poet describes breasts that outdo an elephant's temples, shake the great mountain, bow Kama's head and make ascetics forget their penance, and asks whether a day will come when, leaving those women's beds, he bows at the golden feet and is called a servant who performs worship. The praise is a picture of Solaimalai: streets ringing with the Vedas and full of sacrificial fires, the thousand-faced stream of the anklet (நூபுர) Ganga at its bathing ghats, towers hung with festoons, gem-set halls and golden mansions bright as the sun.
1312.nuance: பூசனைசெய் தொண்டன் என்பது ஒருநாளே: the wish is to be named a servant who worships, a public identity rather than an inner state. The praise is a rare town-portrait; நூபுரம் இரங்கு கங்கை names the hill's stream as the Ganga of the anklet. The first lines of the plea are hard to divide.

1313.reading: In the language of yoga the poet traces an ascent: from the four-petalled lotus with the breath running on both sides, through the centres of earth and the others, the three regions, the light of a hundred and eight petals, bindu and nada and the sound beyond, through the sacred Nandi; he asks Murugan to make him, a mute one, shine, to send him out by the root gate into the light on Murugan's breast, and give him today the way the eight kinds of yoga join in this. The praise names Siva who sold horses as a horse-merchant and took Vadavurar as his servant, Gauri on his left who cut the seven births, and a long list of shrines, Kasi, Rameswaram, Ratnagiri, Kanchi, Madurai, Thiruthani, Senthil, Nagai, Kazhi, Palani and Navalur, with the hill of Solaimalai.
1313.nuance: The terms are those of the yogic body: நாலு சதுரக் கமலம் (the four-petalled root centre), இரு பக்கம் செல் வளி (the two breaths), விந்து நாத, மூல வாசல், யோக பேதவகை எட்டு (the eight limbs). The splitting of the numbers (ஆர மூணு பதி, நுறு பத்தினுடன் எட்டு இதழ்) is unsure. வாசி வாணிகன் எனக் குதிரை விற்று ... வாதவூரன்: Siva as horse-dealer for Manikkavasagar, named by his town. The shrine list repeats the device of the catalogue song 1306.

1314.reading: The poet traces his life: formed in the mother's womb with limbs, mouth, eyes, nose and ears, falling into the hands of grey-haired women, laid to sleep and fed on the mother's breast, then taking wife, kin, a life that does not last and wealth as permanent, never thinking of Murugan; he asks whether a day will come when this utter fool, who never learned to worship the feet, is made to sing Murugan's praise and reach true knowledge. The praise shows the battlefield where ghosts with jackals drink the demons' blood and owls dance, and names Murugan who embraces the girl raised by the elephant and the hunter girl, lord of the devotees at the hill of golden terraces and cloud-touched groves.
1314.nuance: The life is told from conception (கருவாகியெ தாய் உதரத்தினில் உருவாகவெ) through birth and nursing to the household, so that the whole course becomes the delusion: சதமாம் இது தானென. நரைமாதர் are the old women, midwives, whose hands first receive the child. The hill is called அலையாமலை.

1315.reading: Built on doubled cries, the song describes women coming with anklets jingling, youths seeking them in endless infatuation, breasts gleaming and the poet's heart lurching, and asks that, at the hour when this seizes him, Murugan say 'Hey, hey! what delusion is this, tell me', and give grace saying 'here, here are the feet you love'. The praise names Murugan younger brother of Ganesha who broke his tusk to write the Bharata on Meru, the guru who taught Tamil in the ear of the great sage, and the Guha whose vel cut Sura as he cried 'we will not yield', with blood gushing, at Solaimalai, with Devayanai's shoulders and twelve arms.
1315.nuance: The whole song is made of doubled exclamations (கலீர் கலீர், பகீர் பகீர், அடா அடா, இதோ இதோ, குபீர் குபீர்), so the grace is imagined as a scolding and a showing in the god's own voice. பாரதத்தை மேரு ... கோடொடித்த: Ganesha's broken tusk used to write the Mahabharata. மாமுநிக்கு காதில் உணர்வு: Tamil taught to Agastya. வாடை பற்று வேளை may be the hour of love's wind or of death; the plea is unsure.

1316.reading: The poet speaks of the body wasted by fevers, phlegm, cough, wheezing and the humours, and asks whether, fattening the dreadful wretched belly with food every day, one can gain the yogic power that prolongs life, or whether, freed from the torment of worldly books and given blissful experience, he will reach Murugan's lotus feet of knowledge that dance the dance of nada in the formless void. The praise names Rama, for whom the son of the wind and Vali's son threw hills to bridge the sea, and who killed the ten-headed one with an arrow, as Murugan's uncle, the peacock that danced on Sura's crushed brains, and Murugan son of Tyagar at Solaimalai where sages and gods gained knowledge.
1316.nuance: உருவிலாத பாழில் வெட்டவெளியில் ஆடு நாத நிர்த்த ... ஞான பாதம்: the feet dance in the formless void, the open space of the yogis. The question on yoga siddhi gained by feeding the body seems ironic. How the halves of the plea join (what is before the diseases come, and what is asked) is unclear. தலைகள் ஆறு நாலு: six and four, ten heads.

1317.reading: The poet lists the courtesans who set a price on their affection, unsettle the minds of those who love them, take bodies through sin, comb and knot their hair, cast infatuation with a look, polish tarnished brass ornaments with ash to make them shine, flaunt jewels at breast and ear, speak lavish lies and cheat and drain even those who love them, and asks whether he will set his mind on their maya and suffer daily. The praise names Valli guarding the millet field with her sling, Siva who went as messenger for the poet who sang him and who was beaten for pittu as a labourer at the Vaigai bank in Koodal, and Murugan who came at the holy town of Pugali, at the ancient Solaimalai thick with sandal and agil trees.
1317.nuance: பாசத்தால் விலை கட்டிய பொட்டிகள் and பித்தளையிற் பணி நீறிட்டே ஒளி பற்ற விளக்கிகள்: love with a price on it, and brass passed off as gold, the fraud put in one picture. திருப்புகலிப் பதி வருவோனே: Murugan who came at Pugali (Sirkazhi), the identification with Sambandar. The Siva stories are Sundarar's messenger and the Madurai pittu labourer. How அடிபடுவோனோ டாரத்தோடு divides is unsure.

1318.reading: In a run of confessions the poet says he has not seen through the illusion of spear-eyed women, has not worshipped with garlands, has not known that the goods that are beginning and end are the six faces, nor that the dancing peacock is the form of the one mantra, that he wanders the world in a body made of nada and bindu and has not stood worshipping in the state of nada; he asks Murugan to rule him by giving the 'I am He' that the life which knows the light is Siva. The praise names Murugan who won over Sura's clan and stands at Solaimalai.
1318.nuance: The plea is all negations (தெளியேனே, பணியேனே, தெரியேனே, அறியேனே). சோதி உணர்கின்ற வாழ்வு சிவம் என்ற சோகம் அது தந்து: சோகம் is likely सोऽहम् 'I am He', the meditation of identity with Siva, though it can also read as grief. The peacock as மந்த்ர ரூபம் makes Murugan's mount a mantra.

1319.reading: The poet describes women whose earrings reach their eyes, who bewilder Kama and are kin even to Death, who destroy great penance, with eyes like mango slices, who call sweetly, give their honey lips and pleasure, then work betrayal and ruin a man's good name, and asks whether their kinship is fit. The praise describes Uma with breasts like golden pots that burst their bodice, the yogini skilled in all things, the peacock-like Uma who bore Murugan, and Murugan who took up the vel and cut down Sura's kin, at Solaimalai.
1319.nuance: மாய நமனுக்கும் உறவாகி: the women are kin to Death himself, desire and death in one person. The praise answers the plea with the same body: Uma's breasts described in the plea's terms, now as the mother's.

1320.reading: With the refrain 'showing', the poet lists the courtesans' displays, loosened hair, rolling eye corners, earrings, love-talk, pale lips, nail marks, swaying breasts, bent waist, loosened clothes and anklet feet, and asks whether he will stop earning for those who buy a man's life for a price. The praise names Murugan who cut off the tuft of Brahma, husband of Saraswati of the Veda face, the Siva who made the crocodile give back the swallowed boy and heard Tamil expounded, the matted-haired lord with the elephant skin and Ganga who bowed to receive grace, and the one who showed him the nature of Siva and made the peacock dance.
1320.nuance: உயிரை விலைகொளும் அவர்க்குத் தேட்டம்: not wealth alone but life is the price. The praise refrain takes the same verb, காட்டி turning to காட்டு: the women show their bodies, Murugan shows Siva his own nature (சிவமயத்தைக் காட்டு). The crocodile story is Sundarar's at Avinashi. The phrases முதல்வ குகைபடு திருப்பொற் கோட்டு முனிநாடா and குலமலை are obscure.

1321.reading: The poet pictures old age: hair grey as a crane, teeth rattling loose, faltering steps with a stick, coughing and hiccupping, vomiting phlegm and bile, then sesame oil boiled with triphala, dry ginger and long pepper, strained and taken, until the body dies; before life goes, he asks to learn Murugan's praise, hold and worship his feet, and be given the supreme release that cuts birth. The praise shows Murugan saddling his mount to ride against Sura's hosts, making the peacock dance in battle, escaping Indra's daughter to give his heart to the hunters' daughter in the millet field, and piercing the cruel hill, the fierce lord who dwells on Kulagiri.
1321.nuance: The remedies (திலதயிலம், திரிபலை, சுக்கு, திப்பிலி) are listed with a physician's care, only to end in உடல் செத்திட்டு: medicine prolongs nothing. The cure asked for is song and the feet. குலிசன் மகட்குத் தப்பியும்: a playful turn, Murugan slipping away from Devayanai to Valli.

links.note: The Kural opens with A as first of letters and God as first of the world; 1307 makes Murugan the letter A itself (அகரமுமாகி), and the one above the three gods.
Both turn into a catalogue of shrines; 1306 is wholly the list, while 1313 sets the list after a yogic ascent, as if the outer pilgrimage answered the inner one.
The Kural warns that the sweet words of women who want wealth, not love, bring harm; 1317 names their lavish lying speech and love set at a price, and adds the brass polished to pass for gold.

The Naladiyar sees the old man with failed speech, a staff and lost teeth still eyeing desire; 1321 gives the same old age in detail, adds the medicines, and draws the remedy not from renunciation but from song and the feet.

The Thiruppugazh hymns Murugan as அயனென ஆகி அரியென ஆகி அரனென ஆகி அவர்மேலாய், becoming Brahma, Vishnu and Hara and standing above them. The Tirumanthiram says of Siva தானே அயன்மால் என நின்று தாபிக்கும், he himself stands as Brahma and Vishnu and establishes things. Both make the highest god the one who becomes the lesser gods; the song adds that he is also above them.

In the Thiruppugazh's long litany of the Goddess whose son Murugan is, the names வயிரவி நீலி stand among Kali, the trident-bearer and Abhirami. The Tirumanthiram's Bhairavi mantra opens with the same pair, நின்ற வயிரவி நீலி நிசாசரி, and bids one proclaim her. The pairing shows Arunagirinathar's Goddess names drawing on the fierce Bhairavi of the Saiva mantra tradition, here made Murugan's mother.

The Thiruppugazh asks Murugan to come performing the dance of knowledge நாரணனும் வேதன் முன்பு தெரியாத, that Narayana and Brahma never knew. The Tirumanthiram tells the story behind the phrase: அடிமுடி காண்பார் அயன்மால் இருவர் படிகண்டிலர், Brahma and Vishnu searched for Siva's foot and crown and did not see his form. The song gives Siva's unseen form to Murugan's dance.

The Thiruppugazh asks for Murugan's ஞான நடம், the dance of knowledge, so that Death does not come near. The Tirumanthiram follows Siva's dance inward, ending in ஞானத்துள் ஆடி முடித்தான், he danced within knowledge and completed it. The Tirumanthiram places the dance inside knowledge; the song asks for that dance to come to the poet as protection from Death.

The Thiruppugazh confesses a heart that wavered for மாது மனையான மைந்தர் சேரு பொருள், wife, house, children and wealth, taking this life as permanent (வாழ்வு சதமாம் இது). The Tirumanthiram mocks people who say of வாழ்வும் மனைவியும் மக்கள் உடன்பிறந்தாரும், 'what limit is there to what is ours?'. Both name the household list and say the error is believing it lasts; the Tirumanthiram's way out is giving, the song's is the feet.

The Naladiyar says a harlot's love is like a lamp's light: விளக்கொளியும் நெய்யற்ற கண்ணே அறுமே, அவரன்பும் கையற்ற கண்ணே அறும். The Thiruppugazh speaks from after that moment: நீடு பொருள் போன பின்பு பாதகனுமாகி நின்று, when the great wealth had gone he stood a sinner. The song takes the Naladiyar's warning past poverty to guilt, the loss the proverb does not count.

Both songs trace the same yogic ascent from the same root: 1313 begins at நாலு சதுரக் கமலம் and reaches விந்து நாத ஓசை, and 506 begins at நாலுசதுரத்த ... மூலகமலம் and reaches the conch sound of விந்துநாதம். The Pazhamudircholai song asks to go out by the மூல வாசல் into Murugan's light, the Chidambaram song to reach the hall of countless dances; the same map ends at Murugan in one and at Siva's dance in the other.

The Thiruppugazh asks Murugan to give today யோக பேதவகை எட்டும் இதில் ஒட்டும் வகை, the way the eight kinds of yoga join in this ascent. The Tirumanthiram names those eight: இயம நியமமே ... தியானஞ் சமாதி அயமுறும் அட்டாங்கம். The song asks as a gift for what the Tirumanthiram sets out as a practice.

The Tirumanthiram says that in the womb (கர்ப்பத்து) maya joins her brood to the soul, thought arises and karma takes firm hold. The Thiruppugazh tells the life that follows, from கருவாகியெ தாய் உதரத்தினில் உருவாகவெ through nursing to wife, kin and wealth taken as சதமாம் இது, permanent. The Tirumanthiram names the bond made in the womb; the song shows it playing out over a whole life.

The Tirumanthiram holds that if the body perishes the life perishes, so உடம்பை வளர்க்கும் உபாயம் அறிந்தே உடம்பை வளர்த்தேன், knowing the means, I nurtured the body. The Thiruppugazh asks whether one can gain யோக சித்தி by fattening உடல்செய் கோர பாழ் வயிற்றை daily with food, and sets its hope on the feet of knowledge instead. If the question is read as ironic, as its wording suggests, the song denies what the Tirumanthiram affirms: that tending the body is the road to the goal.

The Thiruppugazh seeks the feet of knowledge that dance in உருவிலாத பாழில் வெட்டவெளியில், the formless void, the open space. The Tirumanthiram crosses the void to reach Nandi's feet and rests in கற்பனை உதறிய பாழில், the void that has shaken off even imagining. Both make the பாழ், the empty void, the place where the feet are found rather than a loss.

The Thiruppugazh lists courtesans who நேசித்தாரையும் எத்தி வடிப்பவர், cheat and drain even those who love them. The Naladiyar's worthless woman ஆமாபோல் நக்கி அவர்கைப் பொருள்கொண்டு, licks like a wild cow and takes the wealth from their hands, then bolts like a buffalo. Both make the affection itself the means of draining the lover; the Naladiyar adds the ridicule that follows.

The Thiruppugazh asks Murugan to rule him by giving சோதி உணர்கின்ற வாழ்வு சிவம் என்ற சோகம், the 'I am He' that the life knowing the light is Siva. The Tirumanthiram says that to those who say சோகம் on the path of union, சிவமாம் அமலன் சிறந்தனன், the stainless Siva stands forth. The pairing supports reading the song's சோகம் as soham, the meditation of identity with Siva, rather than as grief.

The Thiruppugazh confesses நாதமொடு விந்துவான உடல் கொண்டு நானிலம் அலைந்து திரிவேனே, wandering the earth in a body made of nada and bindu, and asks for சிவம் என்ற சோகம். The Tirumanthiram makes the same link a method: lives come from விந்துவும் நாதமும், and விந்து அடங்க விளையும் சிவோகமே, when bindu is contained Sivoham grows. What the song asks as a gift, the Tirumanthiram makes the fruit of restraining bindu.

The Kural's lover says பண்டறியேன் கூற்றென்பதனை இனியறிந்தேன், he never knew Death before and now knows it, in a woman's battling eyes. The Thiruppugazh calls the women மாய நமனுக்கும் உறவாகி, kin even to Death. The Kural's lover is overwhelmed by desire; the song makes the same identity of woman and Death a warning.

The Kural says பொருட்பெண்டிர் பொய்ம்மை முயக்கம் is like embracing a stranger's corpse in a dark room. The Thiruppugazh lists every display of the courtesans with the refrain காட்டி, showing, and calls them those who உயிரை விலைகொளும், buy a man's life for a price. Both say the embrace is false and paid for; the song makes the price life itself, not wealth alone.
